title: ZDX API conventions: time ranges, paging, reporting delay and how API numbers differ from the console
aliases: zdx api does not match ui

prose.text: Most ZDX report and alert endpoints take a time window as `from` and `to` in epoch seconds and page with an opaque offset. The per-endpoint parameters are in the contract (`vendor/zscaler-api-specs/automate-zscaler/openapi/zdx.openapi.json`); this subject gathers the rules that apply across them.

prose.label: Time ranges.
prose.text: The 2-hour default is [[zdx.reports:default-window]], and most report reads take at most 2 hours per request while a few need no range, [[shared.log-export.zdx:two-hour-window]]. The alert endpoints' limits are in [[zdx.alerts]]. How far back a request may reach, and whether probe IDs age out, is open {{gap:look-back-limit}}. The Python `since` shorthand is [[zdx.sdk-python.request-shaping:since-to-epoch]] and the Go filter struct [[zdx.sdk-go:epoch-filters]].

prose.label: Paging.
prose.text: Paged lists return a `next_offset` to send back as `offset`, [[zdx.reports:paging]]. The Python response object's own paging does not return ZDX records: [[zdx.sdk-python.response-models:paging-reads-items]].

prose.label: Reading the numbers.
prose.text: The reporting delay is [[shared.log-export.zdx:reporting-delay]]; how API values relate to the console, and what a score of -1 means, is [[shared.log-export.zdx:api-vs-ui]].

checks.do: Whether a report request's window is 2 hours or less, or was split into 2-hour requests.
Whether the most recent 20 minutes are missing because of the reporting delay rather than a fault.
Whether a paged list was followed to a null `next_offset` by hand rather than with the Python response object's `next()`.

look-back-limit.title: How far back a ZDX report request may reach, and whether probe IDs expire
look-back-limit.detail: The 2-hour default, the 2-hour window for most report endpoints and a 14-day limit on the alert endpoints are documented; no source states the oldest `from` a report endpoint accepts, or whether a web or cloud-path probe ID read in one window remains valid later. Unverified legacy statement: no maximum is stated for device and application metric endpoints, and in practice large ranges may time out.
look-back-limit.blocks: planning historical report pulls and reusing probe IDs
